title: Ethiopian Christmas Chicken
community: Ethiopian Orthodox Christians — the Christmas (January 7th) chicken
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Genna Doro — the Christmas Doro Wat, prepared for Ethiopian Christmas (January 7th). Same as the great Doro Wat but combined with Ye-Beg Key Wat on the same mesob platter. The Christmas morning feast that follows the overnight Genna church service.
longDesc: Genna (Ethiopian Christmas) Doro is the Doro Wat prepared for Christmas morning — made after the 43-day Advent fast, served as the breaking of the fast alongside lamb Key Wat. The combination of chicken and lamb on the Christmas mesob is the most complete Ethiopian celebration feast of the year.
ingredients: // Full Doro Wat recipe — see ETH061
// Prepare exactly as ETH061 — the Christmas version uses the same proportions
// Serve alongside Ye-Beg Key Wat (ETH041) on the Christmas mesob
steps: Make simultaneously with Ye-Beg Key Wat (ETH041) for the Christmas platter.
Both must be ready to serve together.
chefTips: Christmas Doro Wat should be made the evening before — serves the morning feast better.
The combination with lamb Key Wat on the same platter is the Christmas tradition.
servedWith: On the full Christmas mesob platter
culturalNote: Ethiopian Christmas (Genna) falls on January 7th and is celebrated with the overnight Genna football game (a traditional stick-and-ball game played at dawn), the church service, and the breaking of the fast with Doro Wat and lamb. The Christmas mesob table is the most complete and most beautiful Ethiopian food experience of the year.
